Contract.title: Bring-up runs as named stages and app_main returns
Contract.Problem: In the firmware project the compile gate proves only that the image builds; it says nothing about bring-up order. Boot behaviour is confirmed only when someone reads the boot log off the board, and app_main loops forever, so nothing marks the end of bring-up.
Contract.Change: app_main runs each component init as a named stage that logs begin and done, logs that all components initialized, and then returns. A stage that fails enters diagnostic idle and names itself.

Constraints.Constraint: Stage deadlines hold as the rule states them.
An absent companion controller is not a boot failure.

NonGoals.NonGoal: The order of component initialization is unchanged.
No component's own init logic changes.

Acceptance.Criterion: The image builds and fits its partition.

A clean boot of the candidate build on the board, with no companion controller attached, logs begin and done for every stage in bring-up order, then that all components initialized, then the return from app_main, with no diagnostic idle and no panic.
The recorded log replays off the bench with the first stage begin, the last stage done and both closing lines in order, and no failure text.

Checks.Environment: development board on the bench, flashed with the candidate build, console on COM7, no companion controller attached.

Decisions.Decision: The live capture CK2 needs the board on the bench; without it the change does not close.

The replay CK3 exercises only the four end markers, in a log captured from BENCH-UNIT-01 during this change, and never substitutes for CK2; that the full marker list matches what the firmware prints rests on CK2 alone. CK3 is optional, so A3 is advisory and does not gate close. It carries no environment, because a recorded log cannot be the candidate build.
The failing-stage path is not provoked on hardware in this change; it is covered only by the Forbid markers staying absent on a clean boot.

E1 declares the companion controller absent, and CK2 then shows companion_init still logs done, which is how the capture reads against K2. The absence is declared by the bench operator, not observed by the capture.
